issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify addGuestStudents(int): void, and the solution implements public void addGuestStudents(int). However the template defines addGuestStudents with a different signature: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). This parameter mismatch can confuse students about which method signature to implement and the intended API, and may cause inconsistencies with instructor tests or the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template method signature match the specification and solution by changing or replacing the template stub to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO */ }. Alternatively, if a boolean validateInput parameter is intended, update the problem statement, UML, and solution to include that parameter consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a method addGuestStudents(int) but the template's Lecture class declares addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). The solution implements addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch in the method signature (extra boolean parameter in the template) creates a direct mapping/confusion for students: they are instructed to implement addGuestStudents(int) while the starter code provides a differently shaped method, which can mislead students and cause test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template method signature to match the problem statement and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } (remove the extra boolean validateInput parameter), so students clearly map the requirement to the provided starter code.
